summary: Abrogans is a Latin word list with Old High German equivalents, and this manuscript, kept in the Abbey Library of St Gallen, is the oldest surviving book in the German language. The glossary fills pages 4 to 289 and was written by at least three scribes. Two pages after it are blank apart from two runic words. Next come a Latin text on church doctrine by Gennadius and, at the very end, the Lord's Prayer and a creed in Old High German.
context: The volume dates to the later eighth century, roughly 765 to 775, and has 323 pages. The glossary lists about 3,670 Old High German words, which makes it a rare window on the earliest written German. Scholars have named Bishop Arbeo of Freising and a monk called Kero as possible authors, and the translation was probably made at Freising. A second copy survives in Paris. The St Gallen manuscript is the best known and is now digitised in full.
